chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He was asked about a man who gives an advance payment (salam) for sheep, specifically two-year-olds and one-year-olds, and other than that, up to a specified term.

He said: There is no problem if the one upon whom is the sheep is not able to provide all of what is upon him, that the owner of the sheep takes half of it, or a third of it, or two-thirds of it, and they take the capital value of what remains from the sheep in dirhams, and they take below their stipulation, and they do not take above their stipulation.
And garments are also like wheat, and barley, and saffron, and sheep.
ai.seo_question: What are the rules for partial delivery in a salam contract if the seller cannot provide the full quantity?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the flexibility of the 'salam' contract in Shia jurisprudence, permitting partial delivery of livestock or agricultural goods when the seller is unable to fulfill the entire obligation. It establishes that the buyer may accept a proportional share of the actual goods and receive the monetary value of the remainder, provided the total compensation does not exceed the agreed-upon terms. This ruling underscores the practical application of fairness in trade, ensuring that neither party is unduly burdened by partial performance.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup>
was asked about the man who submitted an advance payment regarding the sheep three year old sheep, and younger, and other than that, up to a named term.

He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘There is no problem if he is not able, the one upon whom is the (provision of) the sheep, upon the entirety of what is upon him, if the owner of the sheep were to take half of it, or a third of it, or two-thirds of it, and he (buyer) takes back the capital wealth of whatever remains from the sheep, as Dirhams, and he takes below his stipulation, and the should not be taking above their stipulation;
and the garments as well as like the wheat, and the barley, and the saffron, and the sheep’.
en.sarwar: Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Once abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, was asked about the case of a man who made and advance payment to buy sheep of three and less than three years old and others for an appointed time.

He (the Imam) said, ‘It is not unlawful if the one who must provide sheep cannot have all that he is responsible for; the buyer can have half, one-third, two-third with the capital of the rest of the sheep in the form of dirhams.
They can take below their condition and not above the condition and this applies to sacks of wheat, barley and saffron and sheep also.’”
